latin.685: ANNOTATIO VI. De Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali Indignorum. §. I. Manducationis corporis Christi Oralis terminum & rationem, etsi plenius, Annotatione præcedente, excussimus; tamen, cùm ex una parte, Lutheranorum emunctoris judicii Theologi, ad terminum hunc, de Indignis quoque prædicandum, prædicatumque, nauseare incipiant, Sacramentalis Manducationis termino in istius locum surrogatô; ex altera parte Reformati quandam corporis Christi Sacramentalem Manducationem, etiam in indignos cadere posse haud abnuant; de hoc Sacramentalis Manducationis termino aliquid hôc locô prælibandum fuerit, antequam vel de Indignis, quibus ista Manducatio tribuitur, vel de Attributionis hujus Veritate & Necessitate, quicquam determinemus.
latin.686: Itaque Manducatio corporis Christi, Sacramentalis, pro Orali supponens, duplici sensu accipi potest, vel hôc, ut denominatio à corpore Christi, ceu Objecto ejus, ei intrinseca sit, ipsámque corporis Christi Substantiam Manducatio attingat; vel istô, ut denominatio eadem Christi corpus extrinsece duntaxat respiciat & Sacramentalis corporis Christi Manducatio audiat, non quòd ipsius corporis Christi Substantialis, sed Sacramenti potiùs hujus Corporis, i. e. panis benedicti, Christi corpus repræsentantis, Manducatio existat.
latin.687: Uti posteriori sensu Manducationem corporis Christi Sacramentalem Oralémque ne Indignis quidem abnuunt Reformati, ita Lutherani Indignis priori quoque sensu, Manducationem corporis Christi Sacramentalem, i. e. Oralem, competere sustinent. De quibus autem Indignis loquatur utraque pars, id proximè dispicendum, ansam disquisitionis suppeditante Apostolô, quando 1. Cor. 11, 27. quosdam indignè corpus Christi manducare profitetur.
latin.688: Sunt autem Indigni Manducantes duplicis generis, VEL INDIGNI ABSOLUTE & respectu totius Christianismi, qui non dignè vivunt Vocatione suâ, quâ vocati à tenebris ad mirabilem Evangelii lucem sunt, ab Apostolo eodem, sub lacrymarum effusione, notanter hôc modo descripti, quòd sunt inimici crucis Christi, quorum exitus est perditio, quorum Venter Deus eorum, quorum honor in turpitudinem definit, eorum qui carnaliter animati sunt, Phil. 3, 19., Verbo uno, impii omnes & hypocritæ, puta habitualiter tales, veris interim in Ecclesia Christianis permixti.
latin.689: VEL INDIGNI SECUNDUM QUID & respectu solius S. Cœnæ adeundæ, qui alioquin habitualiter pii, in peccatum, tamen contra conscientiam, ex imbecillitate quadam carnis, lapsi, S. Domini cœnam accedunt, non ante exploratis satis se ipsis, i. e. pœnitentia sufficienti, peccatis suis deletis, in Sanguine Christi, fide viva sibi applicato.
latin.690: De posterioribus hisce ex professo egit Apostolus, dictô ad Corinthios capite, dicens, quòd manducando de pane Sacro, bibendóque de poculo, ipsius corporis Christi rei fiant, & judicium, ad minimum temporale, sibi edant & bibant, i. e. in morbos graviores incidant, subsequente quandoque ipsâ morte temporali, eam planè ob causam, quòd non discernunt corpus Christi, vel ad sacrum epulum non aliter advolant, quàm ad communem cibum manducandum.
latin.691: Etsi verò Reformati Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem in universum inficiantur, à quocunque, digno, seu indigno, dicatur fieri; tamen quando de Indignorum corporis Christi Manducatione Orali, cum Lutheranis disputant, prioris generis Indignos potissimum respiciunt, indigitantes, hujusmodi Indignos, i. e. habitualiter impios ac irregeneratos, nullô planè modo, eóque nec Orali Manducatione, ipsius corporis Christi, in S. Cœna fieri participes.

pass_a.685: ANNOTATION VI. On the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body by the Unworthy. §. I. Although we more fully examined the term and reason of Oral Eating of Christ’s body in the preceding Annotation; yet, since on one side Lutheran theologians of clearer judgment begin to nauseate at this term as also to be predicated of the Unworthy, and predicated, a term of Sacramental Eating being substituted in its place; and on the other side the Reformed hardly deny that a certain Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body can fall even on the unworthy — something must be tasted here of this term Sacramental Eating, before we determine anything either about the Unworthy to whom that Eating is attributed, or about the Truth and Necessity of this Attribution.
pass_a.686: Therefore Eating of Christ’s body, Sacramental, standing for Oral, can be taken in a double sense: either thus, that the denomination from Christ’s body as its Object is intrinsic to it, and the Eating touches the very Substance of Christ’s body; or thus, that the same denomination regards Christ’s body only extrinsically and is called Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body, not because it is Substantial of Christ’s body itself, but rather Eating of this Body’s Sacrament — i.e. of the blessed bread representing Christ’s body.
pass_a.687: As in the latter sense the Reformed do not deny even to the Unworthy Sacramental and Oral Eating of Christ’s body, so the Lutherans maintain that to the Unworthy also in the former sense Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body — i.e. Oral — belongs. But of which Unworthy each side speaks must next be examined, the Apostle supplying the handle of inquiry when at 1 Cor. 11:27 he professes that some eat Christ’s body unworthily.
pass_a.688: Now Unworthy Eaters are of a double kind: EITHER UNWORTHY ABSOLUTELY and in respect of whole Christianity, who do not live worthily of their Calling by which they are called from darkness to the marvelous light of the Gospel — described by the same Apostle under pouring of tears notably thus, that they are enemies of Christ’s cross, whose end is perdition, whose Belly is their God, whose honor ends in shame, of those carnally minded, Phil. 3:19 — in one word, all the impious and hypocrites, namely habitually such, meanwhile mixed among true Christians in the Church.
pass_a.689: OR UNWORTHY IN A QUALIFIED SENSE and in respect only of approaching the Holy Supper — who otherwise habitually pious, yet having fallen into sin against conscience from some weakness of the flesh, approach the Lord’s holy supper without first examining themselves enough, i.e. with sufficient repentance, their sins deleted in Christ’s Blood applied to themselves by living faith.
pass_a.690: Of these latter the Apostle treated expressly in the said Corinthian chapter, saying that by eating of the Sacred bread and drinking of the cup they become guilty of Christ’s body itself, and eat and drink judgment to themselves — at minimum temporal — i.e. fall into heavier diseases, sometimes followed by temporal death itself, plainly for this cause: that they do not discern Christ’s body, or fly to the sacred feast no otherwise than to eat common food.
pass_a.691: But although the Reformed deny Oral Eating of Christ’s Body universally, by whomsoever, worthy or unworthy, it is said to be done; yet when they dispute with Lutherans about Oral Eating of Christ’s body by the Unworthy, they chiefly regard Unworthy of the former kind, pointing out that such Unworthy — i.e. habitually impious and unregenerate — in no way at all, and so neither by Oral Eating, become partakers of Christ’s body itself in the Holy Supper.

685: Annotatio VI opens on Oral eating of Christ’s body by the unworthy. §.I first pauses the term itself.

Clearer Lutheran judges are sick of predicating “Oral” of the unworthy and swap in “sacramental eating”; the Reformed allow some sacramental eating can fall on the unworthy — so Strimesius prelibates that term before settling who the unworthy are, or whether the attribution is true and necessary.
686: Sacramental eating (standing for Oral) has two senses.

Intrinsic: the name reaches Christ’s body as object and touches its substance. Extrinsic: it only regards Christ’s body from outside — eating the sacrament of that body, the blessed bread that represents it.
687: Reformed deny the unworthy neither sacramental nor oral eating in the extrinsic sense; Lutherans hold the unworthy also have the intrinsic (true Oral) sense.
Next: which unworthy each side means — the Apostle’s handle is 1 Cor. 11:27, some eating the body unworthily.
688: Unworthy eaters come in two kinds. First: unworthy absolutely, toward whole Christianity — not living worthily of the call from darkness into the Gospel’s light.
Paul describes them with tears (Phil. 3:19): enemies of the cross, belly their god, honor ending in shame — in a word, habitual impious and hypocrites mixed among true Christians.
689: Second: unworthy in a qualified sense, only as to approaching the Supper.

Otherwise habitually pious, they have fallen against conscience by fleshly weakness and come to the Lord’s table without enough self-examination — without sufficient repentance and sins wiped in Christ’s blood by living faith.
690: Paul’s Corinthian chapter treats these latter expressly: eating the sacred bread and drinking the cup, they become guilty of the body and eat/drink judgment — at least temporal sickness, sometimes death.
Cause: they do not discern Christ’s body, or rush the sacred meal as if it were common food.
691: The Reformed deny Oral eating of Christ’s body for anyone, worthy or unworthy.

Yet when they dispute Lutheran Oral-of-the-unworthy, they mainly mean the absolute kind — habitual impious and unregenerate — who in no way, Oral included, partake Christ’s body itself in the Supper. Stop §.I before §.II.
